narr: An upper-level trough west of the region focused a series of short-wave troughs across the local area. The upper-level forcing combined with high moisture combined with a low level 850 mb jet of 35 kts enhanced morning convection across NE FL. Isolated strong to severe storms expanded north and east across NE FL and SE GA into the afternoon and evening.
ev: Flash flooding occurred within the Ocala city limits from about 5-6 inches of rainfall during the morning hours during about a 3 hour accumulation period. The first flash flood report to the NWS was at 9:42 am when Marion county dispatch reported that 3 lanes of traffic were closed on Southeast 17th Street near Southeast Lake Weir Avenue. At 10:15 am, a local newspaper reported that East Silver Springs Blvd, west of South Pine Avenue, was flooding with some portions of the road closed due to flood water. At 10:34 am, the public reported a car was stuck in flood water under bridge on U.S. Highway 441 south of Southeast 3rd Avenue. Around 3 to 4 inches of rainfall was measured in this area around the time of this report since about 8 am. Police and emergency vehicles were on scene. On 6/21 around 9:32 am, law enforcement reported that County Road 475A (SW 27th Avenue) in Ocala was closed due to flood water from SW 66th Street to SW 42nd Street.
